name: Libsyn
description: Libsyn is a podcast hosting, publishing, distribution, analytics, and monetization platform. Creators and media organizations use it to host audio and video, publish episodes, manage feeds and destinations, measure audiences, and operate advertising or subscription programs.
agentUseSummary: Libsyn cannot yet be connected through Relay. Libsyn advertises API access for Professional and Enterprise customers and documents a customer-created WordPress Publisher Hub integration, but it does not publish a distributable product API contract that defines third-party app registration, endpoints, scopes, token lifecycle, show binding, or safe automation rights for a general Relay connector.

blocked.label: Connect Libsyn
blocked.description: No public general-purpose Libsyn API application, scope, token, revocation, endpoint, or least-privilege show-binding contract is available for Relay to implement.

blocked.label: Read private podcast content
blocked.description: Private episodes, drafts, media, show settings, destinations, feeds, transcripts, subscribers, analytics, advertising, and monetization data remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Publish or distribute content
blocked.description: Uploading media, creating or changing episodes, publishing, scheduling, feed mutation, destination delivery, video distribution, and third-party submission are blocked.

blocked.label: Administer shows or monetization
blocked.description: Show, user, plan, billing, advertising, subscription, analytics, destination, dynamic-content, and enterprise administration are blocked.

blocked.label: Use private Libsyn interfaces
blocked.description: Publisher Hub credentials, arbitrary or private APIs, browser automation, session cookies, scraping, RSS bulk ingestion, raw exports, and undocumented endpoints are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Libsyn action is enabled before a contracted product API, exact show boundary, least-privilege authority, content and analytics fields, publishing workflow, and distribution rights are approved.

providerSetup.blocker: Libsyn advertises API access only in its Professional and Enterprise offering and does not publish the corresponding general product API documentation, app-registration process, endpoint catalog, OAuth scopes, token lifecycle, rate limits, show-resource binding, or third-party distribution terms. Its public Publisher Hub instructions expose client credentials created for one WordPress site and a Libsyn user consent session, which is a specific provider-supported integration rather than authorization to repurpose those credentials for Relay. Public RSS and the optional item-ID feed flag provide already-published content, not customer-account authority for drafts, analytics, media, publishing, distribution, monetization, or administration.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, content, distribution, analytics, monetization, legal, privacy, security, and customer owners must choose one bounded outcome and representative contracted Libsyn account. Obtain current official Professional or Enterprise API and commercial terms from Libsyn, then freeze the application ownership, authentication and revocation lifecycle, exact show IDs, fields, episode states, media sources, destinations, analytics granularity, subscriber and advertising exclusions, publication approvals, scheduling, retention, audit, rollback, deletion, rate, and termination rules. Only after that may Relay implement typed bounded wrappers and provider acceptance.

evidence.supports: Libsyn advertises API access as a Professional and Enterprise feature alongside advanced analytics, dynamic advertising, onboarding, and other contracted capabilities rather than as a publicly self-service developer product.

Libsyn documents client ID and secret issuance for one managed WordPress Publisher Hub integration followed by Libsyn login, user consent, and show selection; it does not document reuse as a general third-party API credential.
Libsyn's public publishing workflow includes media upload, episode metadata, release state and distribution behavior that require an explicit bounded automation contract.
Libsyn documents a special public RSS flag for retrieving already-published item IDs and explicitly frames it as a custom-feed integration, not private account or publishing authority.

Libsyn's terms prohibit automated access to site material by scraping or equivalent methods not purposely made available and place content, distribution, and third-party rights obligations on the customer.
